question: What claim about agency is at stake in asserting that the yoginī named Will is established up to Māyā by the siddhas through supreme will?
premises: A yoginī named Will is named.
She is established up to Māyā.
This is done by the siddhas through supreme will.
inference: The yoginī Icchākhyā is established up to the limit of Māyā by the siddhas acting through supreme will.
uncertainties: The precise relation between siddhaiḥ and para-icchayā is syntactically open.
plain_english: The yoginī named Will, by the siddhas through supreme will, reaches up to Māyā.
